planningRules.rule: Never supply, adjust or round an amount. Every figure on an invoice is calculated by the API in one fixed order — structure, less concession, less credit, split by installment, plus late fee, plus tax (BR-1, BR-2) — and a number a planner supplies is money charged to a family that no rule produced.
Never supply the issue date or the due date. Overdue tracking and any late fee run from the due date (BR-7 of UC-04-15), so a date invented here decides when families start being chased and fined.
Never chain an issue onto a preview. The preview is what the office checks before charging anybody; a plan that previews and issues in one run removes the check the two-step shape exists to provide.

Report the excluded students by name and reason. A student with no approved structure, not yet placed, or already billed for the period is excluded and listed rather than aborting the run (BR-3, BR-12, BR-14) — and a preview reported as a clean total hides them.
Never approve a structure to make a preview complete. NO_APPROVED_STRUCTURE means the price list for that class has not been agreed, which is a decision by a different person under UC-04-01.
branch_id and session_id come from $session.

reversal.statement: A preview creates no invoice and moves no money, so there is nothing to reverse. An unwanted preview batch is simply not issued.

steps.note: One step, over a batch that has already been previewed. The invoices, their lines, the credit drawdown, the concession drawdown and the ledger postings all happen inside it, per student, atomically (BR-15).

plan.onFailure: Stop and report. Authorisation, a duplicate run for the same scope and period, and a ledger posting that fails for one student are all enforced by the API and arrive as errors. A school-wide run is not refused — it is held for authorisation (E6), which is an outcome to report.
plan.atomicity: Two guarantees, and they matter separately. **Per student it is atomic**: the invoice, its lines, the credit drawdown, the concession drawdown and the ledger postings are all created or none are, so a credit is never consumed without a bill to show for it (BR-15, E7). **The batch is not**: a student whose posting fails is listed and the rest are issued. Invoice numbers are gapless and never reused, and a failed run consumes none (BR-13). The messages to guardians are separate again and do not block (E10). Report all three layers.

errors.note: Not a failure. Report that the batch is with the School Admin and nothing has been charged (AC-11). Never split the scope to get round it.

errors.written: Nothing for that student — no invoice, no credit drawn, no concession drawn (BR-15).
errors.note: Listed under failed with the reason. Every other student is issued.

errors.note: The credit is drawn down once and a second run applies only what remains (AC-9). Re-preview rather than retrying blind.

errors.notWritten: Some families have not been sent their bill.

planningRules.rule: Never supply, adjust or round an amount. Every figure on an invoice is calculated by the API in one fixed order — structure, less concession, less credit, split by installment, plus late fee, plus tax (BR-1, BR-2) — and a number a planner supplies is money charged to a family that no rule produced.

Report the batch total and the student count before the plan is emitted. Issuing charges every family in the run, sends them a bill, draws down their credits and posts to the ledger — and an issued invoice is never edited (BR-16).
Never issue a batch that was not previewed, and never re-preview and issue in one plan. The preview is what somebody checked; issuing something calculated in the same breath means nobody looked.

Never split a school-wide run into class-sized ones to avoid authorisation. The threshold exists so a School Admin sees a school-wide charge before it goes (BR-9); four class runs bill the same families with nobody having looked.

Report the three layers separately — issued, failed, and whose message did not arrive. A run reported as a single success hides both the students BR-15 refused to half-create and the families who never received a bill.
Never re-emit after ALREADY_ISSUED. The same fee is not billed twice for the same period (BR-14), and the answer is the batch that already exists.
branch_id and session_id come from $session.

reversal.statement: fee.batch.reverse reverses every unpaid invoice in the run as a unit and returns any credit the run applied to the family code (A7). Paid invoices are refused and listed, because money received is not undone by reversing a bill — those go through cancellation or credit under UC-04-08 and UC-04-10. This is a compensating act somebody decides on, never one the controller performs after a failure.

intent.name: fee.batch.reverse
intent.summary: Reverse a whole fee run raised in error, unbilling every unpaid invoice in it and returning any credit it drew. One step, and paid invoices are refused.

routesElsewhere.note: Money received is not undone by reversing a bill. A wrong charge already paid is credited, and an unused credit is refunded.

request.text: bill dobara banao

routesElsewhere.note: A reversal does not re-bill. Raising the run correctly is a fresh preview and a fresh issue.

steps.note: One step. Every unpaid invoice in the batch is reversed as a unit and any credit the run applied is returned to the family code; paid invoices are refused and listed (A7, BR-11).

plan.onFailure: Stop and report. Paid invoices in the batch are refused and listed rather than aborting the reversal — money received is not undone by reversing a bill.
plan.atomicity: The unpaid invoices are reversed as a unit, with the credit and concession the run drew returned to the family code and the ledger entries reversed — together or not at all. Paid invoices are untouched and listed, so a batch containing both leaves a mixed state that is the correct outcome, not a partial failure. The invoice numbers consumed are not reused (BR-13). Guardians already sent a bill are not automatically told it was withdrawn — report that.

errors.note: Listed under refused. Not a failure — it is A7 working. Those go through cancellation or credit under UC-04-08 and UC-04-10. UC-04-02 defines no E-id for it; see OPEN-QUESTIONS.

errors.note: UC-04-02 defines no E-id for it — see OPEN-QUESTIONS.

planningRules.rule: Never compose the reason. A whole run withdrawn is read back later by whoever asks why a class was billed and then unbilled.
Report what the batch contains before the plan is emitted — how many invoices, how many already paid, and the total. A reversal withdraws bills families have already been sent.

Never chain a credit or a refund onto the refused invoices. Money received is not undone by reversing a bill (A7); crediting a paid charge is UC-04-10, with its own approval, and refunding is UC-04-11.
Never chain a fresh run onto a reversal. Re-billing correctly is a new preview somebody checks and a new issue somebody authorises.
Report the families who were sent a bill that has now been withdrawn. Nothing tells them automatically, and a parent holding a challan for a reversed invoice will take it to the bank.

reversal.statement: A reversal is not undone. Re-billing is a fresh preview and a fresh issue, with new invoice numbers — the reversed ones are never reused (BR-13). The controller must not attempt a compensating call.
